question: What does createPortal do in React?

options.text: Opens a new browser window and renders the component there
options.explanation: createPortal renders in the DOM of the current page, not in a new window.

options.text: Creates a new React context for passing data down the tree
options.explanation: That describes createContext, not createPortal.

options.text: Renders a React component into an arbitrary DOM node outside the parent hierarchy
options.explanation: createPortal(children, container) renders children physically into container (e.g., document.body), but the component remains part of the React tree.

options.text: Creates a lazy component that loads on demand
options.explanation: That describes React.lazy, not createPortal.

question: You open a modal, but it's not visible — covered by another element. What most likely happened?

options.text: You need to add display: block to the modal
options.explanation: The problem is CSS stacking context of the parent container, not the modal's display.

options.text: isOpen is set to true, but React hasn't updated the DOM yet
options.explanation: React synchronously updates the DOM before the next render. If isOpen=true, the component is already in the DOM.

options.text: The modal renders inside an element with overflow: hidden or a stacking context with a low z-index
options.explanation: A modal inside overflow: hidden is constrained by that container, and z-index only works within a single stacking context. createPortal into document.body solves this problem.

options.text: React doesn't support z-index above 1000
options.explanation: React doesn't limit z-index values — it's a browser CSS property with no upper limit.

question: Which of the following is NOT preserved for a component rendered via createPortal?

options.text: Application of CSS properties (overflow, z-index) of parent DOM nodes
options.explanation: Physically the portal is in document.body, so parent CSS (overflow: hidden, z-index) doesn't affect it. This is the primary purpose of portals.

options.text: Event bubbling through React parents
options.explanation: Events bubble through the React tree, not the DOM tree. A click inside the portal will reach the React parent.

options.text: Access to React Context from parent components
options.explanation: Context is preserved — the portal remains part of the React tree, despite being in a different place in the DOM.

options.text: Physical position of the DOM node inside the parent container
options.explanation: The portal's DOM node is in the target container (document.body), not inside the component's DOM parent.

question: What is the difference between a layout component and a component with business logic?

options.text: A layout component knows WHERE to place content but doesn't know WHAT that content is. A business component knows WHAT to display but doesn't manage its own placement
options.explanation: This is separation of concerns (SoC). Layout handles structure, business component handles content.

options.text: Layout components are written only in CSS Grid/Flexbox, while business components use other CSS techniques
options.explanation: The difference is conceptual (SoC), not technical. Layout components can use any CSS techniques.

options.text: Layout components always use children, while business components receive data through props
options.explanation: This is partially true but not a complete definition. Business components can also use children.

options.text: A layout component cannot have state, while a business component can
options.explanation: A layout component can have state (e.g., sidebar open/closed state). The difference is in responsibility, not in the presence of state.

question: A user opened two modals. On pressing Escape the first one closed, but page scrolling was unlocked — the second modal is still open. What went wrong?

options.text: Escape should only be bound to the topmost modal in the stack
options.explanation: This is correct for close logic, but doesn't explain the scroll problem.

options.text: Each modal independently manages overflow: hidden without accounting for the number of open modals
options.explanation: Scroll should only be unlocked when all modals are closed. Solution: a counter of open modals or checking that none remain open.

options.text: document.body.style.overflow doesn't work in useEffect
options.explanation: This works correctly. The problem is in the logic of counting open modals.

options.text: You should use a CSS class on body instead of inline style
options.explanation: The way the style is applied (class or inline) doesn't affect the logical error with counting.
